item.title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: Using the diff, terminal, and browser
item.description: The GitHub Copilot app now includes built-in panels that allow developers to review, run, and preview AI agent-generated code without switching between tools. The diff panel displays added, removed, or changed lines with green and red highlighting, letting users accept changes, leave comments, or request modifications from Copilot. The terminal panel enables running commands directly within the session, including dev server scripts started via a Run button, and supports multiple terminal windows simultaneously. For projects with user interfaces, the browser panel allows previewing the application and using the Pick & Polish tool to select elements and iterate with the agent. After confirming changes work correctly across all three panels, developers can accept the changes and create a pull request directly from the app, completing the full review loop in one place.

item.title: Marketing ops as code: Automating events from planning to follow-up on GitHub
item.description: Tomoko Tanaka, who leads marketing for GitHub in Japan and Korea, automated her team's event workflows using GitHub Copilot and existing GitHub primitives. Each event begins as a GitHub Issue created through a conversation with Copilot, which reads a Markdown runbook called AGENTS.md to follow team naming conventions and draft invitation emails. Once an event-setup label is applied, GitHub Actions workflows duplicate the landing page, generate UTM-tagged URLs, create invitation emails, open request issues with other teams, and populate project boards. A daily cron-triggered workflow screens registrants against criteria for invite-only events, while a DRY_RUN repository variable allows the team to rehearse workflows safely without touching external systems. After events, slash commands like /lead-upload and /event-report, powered by SKILL.md Markdown procedures, handle CRM uploads and reporting in the same place everything else lives.

item.title: GitHub availability report: August 2026
item.description: GitHub experienced five incidents in August 2026 that degraded performance across its services. Two major outages occurred: one on August 6 lasting approximately 9 hours primarily impacting GitHub Actions and dependent features like Copilot and Dependabot, and another on August 17 lasting roughly 6 hours 44 minutes that affected Issues, pull requests, and numerous services routing through an overloaded datacenter. Both incidents were triggered when routine operations pushed already capacity-constrained systems past their limits, with the August 17 failure amplified by a latent client retry bug and a service-mesh sidecar that failed to scale. GitHub made progress on long-term improvements, including running production MySQL primaries from Azure, moving authentication services off an aging shared database, and adding headroom to constrained clusters. The company also enhanced monitoring, with automated high-impact incident detection launching on August 21. Work continues on database migrations, service migration to Azure, and building more durable capacity and isolation.

item.title: AURA: Unified Multimodal Framework for Conversational Music Editing
item.description: AURA is a unified multimodal framework for conversational music editing that interprets full dialogue histories along with optional images and reference audio to capture editing intent. A multimodal large language model distills this intent into compact concept tokens, which a concept-to-audio module then injects into a frozen MusicGen backbone alongside frame-aligned reference features. This design enables precise edits while keeping unaffected content intact, optimizing only 91M parameters against 1.9B frozen backbone parameters. Experiments on the Slakh2100 and MoisesDB datasets show substantial gains in edit correctness and content preservation over existing instruction-guided methods. Notably, AURA achieves a four-to-five-fold reduction in FAD for out-of-domain addition and removal tasks.

item.title: Biquaternionic Space with Complex-valued Attention for Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion
item.description: Rushan Geng and Cuicui Luo propose BSCA (Biquaternionic Space with Complex-valued Attention), a temporal knowledge graph embedding model designed to infer missing facts in knowledge graphs that evolve over time. The authors note that many existing models rely on a single geometric space, which limits their ability to represent diverse relational patterns, or treat entity representations as static. To address these limitations, BSCA combines circular and hyperbolic rotations within a unified biquaternionic framework, while a complex-valued attention mechanism adaptively fuses time-conditioned and relation-conditioned entity representations that vary with temporal and relational context. Experiments conducted on five benchmark datasets show competitive performance across all datasets. The largest improvement appears on the GDELT dataset, where BSCA achieves a mean reciprocal rank of 52.1%, compared to 38.1% for the strongest baseline in the authors' comparison.

item.title: SpermYOLO: A Coordinated YOLO-Based Detector for Accurate and Efficient Sperm and Impurity Detection in Microscopic Images
item.description: SpermYOLO is a YOLOv11-derived detection framework designed for joint sperm and impurity detection in microscopic images used in computer-assisted semen analysis. The model incorporates four architectural improvements: C3k2-IDB for channel-wise discriminative feature extraction, D2SEM for spatial-spectral semantic enhancement, MFM for adaptive multi-scale feature fusion, and a DESD Head for detail-enhanced shared prediction. On the SVIA semen microscopic imaging benchmark, SpermYOLO achieves 97.2% sperm AP and 75.4% impurity AP, improving sperm AP, impurity AP, mAP50, and mAP50:95 by 1.6, 10.0, 5.8, and 2.7 percentage points over the baseline while maintaining a lightweight design. Cross-scene evaluation on the SDTB testicular-biopsy microscopy benchmark shows the model reaches the highest mAP50 of 74.8% and mAP50:95 of 31.2%, demonstrating effectiveness with small sperm targets and complex tissue backgrounds. Ablation studies and qualitative analyses confirm the contributions of each module.

item.title: ATTRICITE: Training an Open 4B Model for Citation Recovery toward Faithful Attribution
item.description: ATTRICITE is an open 4B-parameter model trained for tool-using citation recovery within the CiteGuard retrieval environment to support faithful attribution in scientific literature. The authors introduce CITEALIGN, a 7,607-instance computer-science dataset drawn from recent publications, along with a 709-instance benchmark split into 410 development instances from 2024 and 299 temporally held-out test instances from 2025. Using GRPO fine-tuning at an inference temperature of 0.7 across three runs, the model improves Qwen3-4B's target-match accuracy from 49.4%±1.5% to 59.8%±0.2%, a gain of 10.4 percentage points. Despite its small size, ATTRICITE outperforms gpt-oss-20b and comes within 3.9 points of GPT-5.4-mini, though Gemma 4 31B IT leads overall at 72.0%±1.0%. The authors treat the published citation as a human attribution signal and use target recovery as a proxy for progress toward faithful attribution, releasing the model and collection pipeline for reproducible research.

item.title: The Attribution-Compression Frontier in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description: Context compression reduces generator input in retrieval-augmented generation, but answer quality alone does not characterize citation attribution. We measure citation attribution across compression methods and budgets, comparing reranking, extractive selection, abstractive summarization, token pruning, and an extract-cluster-rewrite construction on ASQA and QASPER under a fixed generator and primary entailment evaluator. On ASQA at a nominal 0.25 budget (achieved compression 0.08), a RECOMP-style compressor's citations score 0.86 precision against its summaries but 0.12 against source spans under our re-attributability protocol. item.title: A 386 PC for Your RP2350
item.description: FRANK 386 is an i386 PC emulator for the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (RP2350), developed by Mikhail Matveev and DnCraptor and based on Chunhui He's Tiny386 project. It emulates a full i386 CPU with optional x87 FPU and supports up to 8MB of RAM using PSRAM, with VGA or HDMI graphics output up to 640x480. The emulator can boot DOS, Windows 3.x, Windows 95, and Linux, and includes sound support for AdLib OPL2, Sound Blaster 16, PC Speaker, Tandy, Covox, and Disney Sound Source. It runs on several RP2350-based boards including the FRANK board, Murmulator (M1 and M2 variants), Olimex PICO-PC, and Waveshare RP2350-PiZero, requiring an SD card, keyboard input, and optional audio output. A runtime disk manager (Win+F12) allows hot-swapping disk images, while a settings menu (Win+F11) lets users adjust memory, CPU generation, sound devices, and other configurations without restarting.

item.title: Show HN: Kinesis – Control your Mac with the Meta Neural Band
item.description: Kinesis is a Mac application that allows users to control their computer using the Meta Neural Band, enabling gestures like swiping between desktops, opening Mission Control, controlling music playback, and using pinch and turn motions to adjust volume or brightness. The app supports custom mappings, includes a setup practice mode, and runs from the menu bar. It is built on previous experimentation with Astra in the neural-band-poc repository. Installation requires macOS 14 or later, Apple Silicon or Intel hardware, and involves downloading the DMG, dragging it to Applications, pairing the band, and granting Bluetooth and Accessibility permissions. To build from source, users need Xcode with Swift 6 and can run the included build script after cloning the repository from github.com/callbacked/kinesis.

item.title: OpenArch – PyTorch implementations of modern LLM architectures
item.description: OpenArch is a GitHub repository containing hand-written PyTorch implementations of modern open-source LLM architectures, designed for clarity and learning rather than performance optimization. Each architecture is implemented in a single readable file based on original papers, technical reports, and references from Sebastian Raschka's LLM Architecture Gallery. The project highlights the structural choices that distinguish modern models, including various attention types like MHA, GQA, MLA, and sliding-window, normalization approaches such as RMSNorm and QK-Norm, positional encodings like RoPE, and decoder configurations including dense and sparse MoE. Currently implemented text models include GPT-2, Llama 2, Llama 3, OLMo 2, DeepSeek R1, Gemma 3, Mistral 3, Llama 4 Maverick, Qwen 3, Kimi K2, GLM 4.5, and GPT-OSS, with PaliGemma as a multimodal model and several others under construction. The repository aims to mirror all 72 architectures from the gallery and welcomes contributor participation to expand coverage.

item.title: SDR–; open source SDR with a patchable signal graph, Rust DSP, web UI
item.description: sdr-- is an open source software-defined radio application featuring a patchable visual signal graph where users connect devices, decoders, displays, and recorders on a canvas. A Rust server performs radio and signal processing while a React interface runs either in a desktop window or browser, allowing the server to operate beside the antenna and connect over the network. The software supports AM, NFM, broadcast FM with stereo and RDS, SSB, and various digital voice modes, and can decode aircraft, ship, amateur, pager, and sensor traffic. It ships with native drivers for RTL-SDR, HackRF, SDRplay, and CR-8, while SoapySDR modules provide support for Airspy, bladeRF, LimeSDR, PlutoSDR, and others. A built-in signal generator enables testing without hardware, and the receiver can be controlled through REST, WebSocket, or MCP interfaces. The project is under active development and licensed under GPL v3 or later.
